quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Intersections ahead.
Road construction.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards immediately ahead. This sign warns you of an upcoming curve to the right.

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when following a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered the intersection on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely across before the light turns red. If you block an intersection, you can be cited.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual things on the road:

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Avoid looking at accidents or unusual things on the road. This slowing down, called "rubbernecking," causes traffic jams.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay further behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay further behind the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: In darkness or poor weather, increase your following distance. This gives you more time to react to hazards you may not see in advance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road changes direction or narrows ahead.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road changes direction or narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a change in road direction or a narrower road ahead. You may see these signs on sharp curves or before narrow bridges.

questions.question: What lane must you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, turn from the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: You can pass if you're in the lane with the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass if you're in the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if you're in the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic in that lane can pass. A solid yellow line means traffic in that lane cannot pass.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the vehicle ahead.
Drive carefully through and don't look at the work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through and don't look at the work.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at construction work. Looking at it, called "rubbernecking," causes traffic jams.

questions.question: If you are in an intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, drive through and clear the intersection as quickly as you can.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is 35 mph after the curve.
Do not drive slower than 35 mph on the curve.
Take the upcoming curve at 35 mph or slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take the upcoming curve at 35 mph or slower.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. Speed advisory signs tell you what speed to use for the upcoming hazard.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Use light braking.
Pump the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use light braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using light braking.

questions.question: If you see a severe dust storm ahead, you should:

options.text: Slow down and pull off the road.
Turn on your high beams.
Keep your speed and stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: In a severe dust storm, check traffic around you, slow down, drive off the highway, and stop as far right as possible. Turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, stay in your vehicle with your seat belt on, and wait for the storm to pass.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear when going down a steep hill.
Speed up going into curves and slow down leaving them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you don't know what's ahead. Braking while in a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that turns in the direction of the arrow are not allowed. In this case, right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment in the road.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment in the road.
questions.explanation: Signs will warn you about workers and equipment ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn allowed on red.
Give the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks where passing is not allowed.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Expect anything to happen.
Expect workers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect anything to happen.
questions.explanation: Construction zones can have unexpected hazards. Drive with extra care to protect yourself, other drivers, and workers.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light:

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and go carefully.
Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look both ways, and proceed with caution.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that vehicles:

options.text: Going both ways may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when you change lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when you change lanes.
questions.explanation: Follow laws, signs, signals, and road markings to prevent road rage. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: In which of the following situations should your wheels not point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or slope.
When parked on a flat road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or slope.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight. If hit from behind, this stops you from moving into oncoming traffic. On a hill or slope, angle your wheels so the car won't roll into traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and go carefully.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from an alley:

options.text: Stop at the sidewalk.
Honk your horn.
The speed limit is 15 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: Stop before the sidewalk when entering the road from an alley or driveway.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must let cross traffic pass if it could cause a crash.
Must only yield to vehicles on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let cross traffic pass if it could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you want to enter. Be ready to stop, but you can go if there is no traffic in your way.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder quickly.
questions.explanation: Check behind you before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road and an oncoming vehicle is coming, you should:

options.text: Slow down and wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop.
Honk to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but a vehicle is coming, slow down and let it pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection if no oncoming vehicles are near.
Where signs and road markings allow passing.
In a curve if no oncoming vehicles are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lots, or alleys. Do not pass in curves or over hills where you cannot see oncoming cars. Only pass where signs and markings permit it and when it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to be alert and proceed with caution. Slow down when you see this light.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not stop like you would at regular roads. Use the merge lane to speed up and match the traffic flow, then merge safely.
